design:
Tier 2. Outward-facing: the Hub sends real work back on the strength of what people typed on GitHub, widens the one place that limits what it may ask of GitHub, and makes one notifying call, a review request. Migration: adds nullable build columns only. Rollback: the columns are read only when PR landing is on, so downgrading drops them and reviews are simply not read.

Decisions (operator, 2026-11-08):
- Only a review that requests changes sends anything back. Comment-only and approving reviews are shown on the build, nothing more. This is a team feature: GitHub refuses 'request changes' from a PR's own author, and the Hub opens PRs under the operator's login, so a solo author's own reviews never send work back.
- Each review is handled once, by its GitHub id, recorded on the build.
- An inline comment is matched to a task by that task's own change (the lines and files it touched), not by the PR's commits, so it works with the squash setting. If several tasks touched the file, it goes to the one that touched the commented line; otherwise to the latest of them pushed.
- A general review body, or a comment on a file no task touched, goes to the latest task pushed, marked unmatched.
- Comments of one review for one task are one send-back; several tasks mean several send-backs.
- When the Hub learns of a review: on slice 1's asks (`sync_pr`, pull_requests.py:895; `refresh`, :974) and on slice 2's interval while CI is pending. There is no new timer.
- Once the PR is ready again with the fixes, the reviewers whose changes-requested reviews sent work back are asked to review again, once per review.
- The Hub never replies, resolves threads, approves or dismisses reviews.
- Testing without a second account: the scratch repository carries a workflow_dispatch workflow that submits a REQUEST_CHANGES review with one inline comment as github-actions[bot], using GITHUB_TOKEN with pull-requests: write. That is a real reviewer who is not the PR's author, the way teams' bots review. If GitHub refuses it, the drive says so and the real-GitHub check of the send-back falls back to a stand-in for the review read only; the operator is told.

CURRENT   PR open -> Hub asks state only -> a person's changes-requested review is invisible to the app
PROPOSED  ask -> new changes-requested review (by id) -> inline comments read -> each matched to a task by its own change -> task approved -> revision_needed with the comments; PR back to draft (slice 1) -> fix approved after checks and agent review -> pushed to the same PR -> ready again when all pushed (+ CI, slice 2) -> reviewers who requested changes asked to look again

The contract (grounded in hub/hub/pull_requests.py, builds.py and models.py on master):
- GitHub reads: `check_gh_call` gains a third read pattern, `_REVIEWS_READ`. It matches exactly `repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<number>/reviews?per_page=100` and `.../pulls/<number>/comments?per_page=100`, with an optional `&page=N` as `_COMMIT_READ` allows (F1146), and nothing else. Replies, thread resolution, review approval or dismissal, and any call with `-X` or extra arguments stay refused by the existing `len(args) == 2` rule. Calls go through `gh()`.
- Review request: `gh pr edit <number> --add-reviewer <login>`. `("pr","edit")` is already in GH_ALLOWED, where only a base change is refused, so no new subcommand is allowed. A test pins that this is the only new use of `pr edit`. For a bot reviewer, the login is the one GitHub reports on the review.
- New function `read_reviews(root, number) -> {reviews, error}` beside `read_pr`. It is blocking, run through `blocking.run` as `read_pr` is, and called on the same asks for each build whose answer state is draft or ready, after `read_pr` and before `check_ci`.
- A review record: `{"id": int, "author": str, "state": "CHANGES_REQUESTED"|"COMMENTED"|"APPROVED"|"DISMISSED", "url": str, "submitted_at": str|null, "outcome": "sent_back"|"comment_only"|"approved"|"dismissed"|"already_handled"|"pr_not_open", "sent_to": [task_id], "re_requested_at": str|null, "comments": [{"id": int, "path": str|null, "line": int|null, "body": str, "url": str, "task_id": str|null, "matched": bool}]}`.
- Migration, named `<next>_requested_changes_come_back.py`, takes the next number after master's head at build time (0170 today; the generated-files build may land first). It adds nullable `builds.pr_reviews` (JSON, the list above), `builds.pr_reviews_read_at` (datetime) and `builds.pr_reviews_error` (text, apart from `builds.pr_error`). It is guarded like 0170; the downgrade drops them.
- Build view: `builds.pull_request_view` gains `reviews`, `reviews_read_at` and `reviews_error`, typed on `BuildPullRequest` (hub/ui/src/api/pullRequests.ts).
- Send-back: reuse `landing_queue._send_back` and the existing reason classes. The history row's reason names the review and carries its link, with origin 'checks'. No new event name, setting or task status.
- Existing guards to relax, each named:
  - the 'nm-ac1' allowed-call set in hub/tests/test_a_build_lands_as_one_pull_request_push.py, which must accept the reviews reads and `pr edit --add-reviewer` and nothing else;
  - the notice test;
  - the fake GitHub in hub/tests/test_the_pr_s_ci_is_the_full_check_read.py and the equivalent fakes of slices 1 and 2;
  - scripts/drive/pr_ci_drive.py's quiet-period gh-call audit, which must still hold.

The shape of `gh api` review and comment output, including outdated comments after later pushes, is unverified; matching uses the comment's recorded path and line at the commit commented on.

open_questions.question: When the Hub learns of a review. Answered (operator, 2026-11-08): (a) on slice 1's asks and slice 2's CI interval only; no timer.
A review body that names no file, or a comment on a file no task touched. Answered (operator, 2026-11-08): (a) the latest task pushed, marked unmatched.
Ask the reviewers who requested changes to look again? Answered (operator, 2026-11-08): (a) yes, automatically, once the PR is ready again.
Resolving threads. Answered (operator, 2026-11-08): (a) never; the reviewer does.

Should a solo author's own comment reviews count, since GitHub refuses 'request changes' from a PR's author? Answered (operator, 2026-11-08): no; this is a team feature and need not fit a solo author.
How is it tested without a second GitHub account? Answered (operator, 2026-11-08: a second account is not workable): a workflow in the scratch repository requests changes as github-actions[bot].
Does GitHub accept a changes-requested review on a draft PR? Not the operator's: the drive records what the scratch repository does.

problem:
A PR build lets people review on GitHub, but nothing reads what they say. Slice 1 asks GitHub only for the PR's state (`read_pr`, `gh pr view --json state,isDraft,mergeCommit`) and acts only on merged or closed. A reviewer who requests changes leaves the PR open and blocking, and the operator has to carry each comment to the right task by hand.

The send-back itself exists: `_send_back` moves an approved task to revision_needed with a report (hub/hub/landing_queue.py, around :2032-2072), and a task leaving approved already returns its build's PR to draft. What is missing is reading reviews, deciding which task each comment belongs to, and sending it back.

The Hub cannot read inline comments today. `GH_ALLOWED` (hub/hub/pull_requests.py:176) holds only pr create/edit/ready/view, and `check_gh_call` (:209-226) allows `gh api` only as a two-argument GET matching `_API_READ` (:181) or `_COMMIT_READ` (:184), so a third read pattern is needed. Even after the fix lands, nothing tells the reviewer it is there, so their changes-requested review keeps blocking the merge.

requirements.statement: While a build's PR is open, whenever the Hub asks GitHub for its state, it also reads the PR's reviews and their inline comments, read only; a failed read is shown on the build with GitHub's error and sends nothing back.
Only a review whose state is 'changes requested' sends a task back; a review that only comments or approves is shown on the build with its author and link, and sends nothing back.

Each review is acted on once: the Hub records the GitHub identifier of every review it has handled on the build, and a later ask finding the same review changes nothing, including after a Hub restart.

An inline comment on a file and line goes to the task of the build whose own change touched that line; when no task touched the line but some touched the file, to the latest of those pushed; this holds with the squash setting, where the PR's commits no longer map to tasks.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-08 (option a): a blocking review with nothing moving is the worst result, so it is never dropped for naming no file; the report says plainly it could not be matched.
requirements.statement: A review's general body, and an inline comment on a file no task of the build touched, go to the latest task pushed, and its send-back marks each such comment as not matched to any change of that task.

A review sends each matched task back once, as one send-back that quotes every comment for it in the reviewer's words, with the reviewer's name, the file and line, and a link to the comment; a review whose comments concern two tasks sends both back.

Reviews by different people are handled independently: each changes-requested review sends back its tasks, a second reviewer's approval does not cancel a first reviewer's request, and a comment already sent back in an earlier review is not sent again.
When the task a comment belongs to is already not approved (sent back for another reason, or being fixed), the comments are added to its notes with the review's link and no second send-back is made.

A builder's fix to a review send-back is checked and reviewed as any task is, and once approved is pushed to the same build branch and PR, as a new commit on it, or replacing the build's single commit under the squash setting; no second PR opens, and the PR returns to ready only when every task is pushed again, and CI has passed in a project that uses slice 2.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-08 (option a): a changes-requested review keeps blocking a merge until its reviewer re-reviews, and nothing else tells the reviewer the fix is there.
requirements.statement: When a PR that had a changes-requested review returns to ready with fixes for it, the Hub asks each reviewer whose changes-requested review sent work back to review again, once per such review; it asks no one else, and a failed request is shown on the build and changes nothing else.

Apart from asking reviewers to review again, the Hub reads reviews only with read requests: it never replies to a comment, resolves a thread, approves or dismisses a review, or requests anything of GitHub beyond what slices 1 and 2 allow; a call outside that list is refused before anything runs.

The build and each task sent back by a review show the review's author and link, the comments sent, whether its reviewer was asked to review again, and when the Hub last read reviews; a review that sent nothing back says why (comment only, approval, already handled, PR not open).

in_scope: Reading reviews and inline comments of an open PR through the GitHub CLI, read only
Matching comments to tasks, and sending those tasks back with the comments
Showing review send-backs on the build and the task
Pushing the fix to the same PR through the existing landing path
Asking the reviewers who requested changes to review again once the PR is ready again (operator, 2026-11-08)
non_goals: Replying to comments, resolving threads, approving or dismissing reviews on GitHub (operator, 2026-11-08: the reviewer resolves)
Merging the PR (a person's decision, as in slice 1)
A timer that waits for reviews (operator, 2026-11-08: on slice 1's asks and slice 2's CI interval only)
Treating comment-only reviews as requests for changes, including the author's own (operator, 2026-11-08: a team feature; it need not fit a solo author)
Reading comments on a PR that is merged or closed
Switching this repository to PR landing; this repository lands by direct merge, so the feature is demonstrated on the scratch repository

summary: When a person requests changes on a build's pull request, the Hub reads their comments and sends each affected task back to its builder, quoting the comments that concern it. The fix goes through the usual agent review and checks and is pushed to the same PR. Once the PR is ready again, the Hub asks the reviewers who requested changes to look again. The Hub never replies in threads, resolves them or approves; a person does. A product feature for teams, where reviewers are other people: GitHub does not let a PR's author request changes on their own PR, and the operator confirmed (2026-11-08) that this is fine. Opt-in with PR landing. Tier 2: outward-facing reads of people's words, plus a migration. Builds after slice 2 (the-pr-s-ci-is-the-full-check), which has landed.

Write the acceptance drive against the contract (the review reads, `pull_request.reviews` on the build, the send-back, the same-PR fix and the review request) and record it failing.

It uses gutohuida/agentweave-pr-scratch (required check ci-check). Add to that repository a workflow_dispatch workflow that submits a REQUEST_CHANGES review with one inline comment (inputs: PR number, path, line, body) as github-actions[bot] (GITHUB_TOKEN, permissions pull-requests: write).

The drive builds a two-task spec with PR landing, waits for CI and a ready PR, and dispatches the workflow on task B's file. It expects B sent back with that comment, A untouched, the fix as a new commit on the same PR, the PR ready again once CI passes, and github-actions[bot] listed as requested again. It also leaves a comment-only review with the operator's own account and expects nothing sent back.

It runs on a dedicated trial Hub with its own port and database; real agent turns bind Haiku; one GitHub login only. First prove that the workflow can request changes. If GitHub refuses, record that and report it to the operator rather than adding a second account. Keep pr_ci_drive.py's quiet-period audit true.
